name: To Spec
summary: Turn a settled conversation into an actionable specification.
intro: Capture what has already been decided, connect it to the codebase, and leave a specification someone can implement.
use: Use after a conversation has enough context to define the work. Atlas synthesizes the existing decisions instead of starting another interview.
modes: Read the conversation, relevant code, domain language, and existing decisions.
Choose the highest useful seam for checking the intended behavior, then confirm it with you.
Save locally using the project’s conventions. Publish to an issue tracker when requested.
prompt: Use atlas-to-spec to turn this conversation into a local spec.
note: Tracker publication follows your project context and authorization.
origin: Adapted from Matt Pocock’s To Spec, with Atlas’s approach to local specifications and tracker publication.

name: To Tickets
summary: Break a specification into useful, connected slices.
intro: Turn a plan, spec, or conversation into tracer-bullet tickets with explicit dependencies.
use: Use when the direction is clear and the next step is making the work executable. Each ticket should deliver an observable slice of behavior.
modes: Start from the provided spec, plan, or current conversation.
Define vertical slices and the tickets that block each one.
Write local ticket files by default; mirror them to a tracker when requested.
prompt: Use atlas-to-tickets to break this spec into local tickets with blocking dependencies.
note: Each ticket should describe a deliverable slice and the work that blocks it.
origin: Adapted from Matt Pocock’s To Tickets, with Atlas’s local ticket templates and publication workflow.

name: HTML UI
summary: Make an interface idea concrete before committing to it.
intro: Explore a product interface as an HTML wireframe or a polished, interactive model.
use: Use when a layout, interaction, or product flow is easier to judge by seeing it. Choose the fidelity that answers the question.
modes: Test hierarchy, layout, and task structure without committing to visual polish.
Show a polished mockup or working product flow, preserving the agreed content and structure.
prompt: Use html-ui in Wireframe mode to explore this settings flow.
note: Choose a mode explicitly when fidelity matters. Model work uses the independently available Design Artifact guidance.
origin: Combines the Wireframe and Prototype methods from Plannotator’s Effective HTML, with small adaptations for Atlas’s skill setup.

name: Atlas Craft
summary: Refine the colors, typography, and layout of a real interface.
intro: Improve the details of a production interface while keeping its accepted identity and foundations.
use: Use when the direction is established and the interface needs better execution. Select one method or combine complementary methods.
modes: Refine palettes and tokens, check rendered contrast, and improve color usage.
Work on font choice, sizing, wrapping, and typographic detail.
Improve spacing, alignment, grouping, responsive behavior, and spatial RTL.
prompt: Use atlas-craft in Type and Layout modes to refine this screen.
note: New visual direction belongs to design work. Craft preserves the project’s accepted identity.
origin: Color, Type, and Layout retain Jakub Krehel’s guides, brought together in one Atlas skill.

name: Atlas Motion
summary: Build motion that makes an interface easier to use.
intro: Construct interface animations and physical interactions with methods suited to the behavior.
use: Use for a transition, animated interface, or a direct manipulation gesture. Animate and Fluid can work together when they serve different parts of the task.
modes: Construct an interface animation or transition.
Handle direct manipulation, momentum, and interruptible springs.
prompt: Use atlas-motion in Animate mode to build this panel transition.
note: Preserve the project’s motion tokens and visual identity. Required capabilities are resolved through the agent’s host.
origin: Combines Emil Kowalski’s guides for animation and physical interaction. Animate includes an adaptation for choosing project tools; the Fluid reference is preserved.

name: Atlas Review
summary: Assess a change against its intent and specialist standards.
intro: Review code, judge static checks, or assess interface motion with a method matched to the question.
use: Use when you need findings and evidence before deciding what to change. Reviewing a change does not, by itself, authorize fixes.
modes: Assess changes against standards and the originating intent.
Run scoped lint and type checks, then judge the findings.
prompt: Use atlas-review in Code mode to assess this diff against the spec.
note: Each method has its own evidence limits. After an authorized fix, recheck the uncertainty that remains.
origin: Code review adapts Matt Pocock’s method, and motion review preserves Emil Kowalski’s guidance. Static review is authored by Atlas.

name: Animated-Driven Frontend
summary: Engineer the runtime behind demanding motion.
intro: Apply frontend engineering knowledge to synchronized scroll sequences, progress gestures, WebGL effects, and rendering performance.
use: Invoke this skill explicitly when motion depends on runtime architecture, shared progress, asset loading, or GPU work.
modes: Coordinate shared progress, seeking, holds, drawing, and synchronized feedback.
Handle WebGL assets, GPU uploads, effects, adaptive quality, and mobile rendering.
Manage ownership, dependencies, loading, failures, and accessible motion.
prompt: Use animated-driven-frontend to assess the runtime for this scroll sequence.
note: Test uncertain effects with a bounded sample before expanding them. Keep one authoritative state for synchronized systems.

name: Writing for Humans
summary: Make substantial prose worth the reader’s effort.
intro: Write, revise, or critique documentation, articles, explainers, and other substantial prose without flattening the author’s meaning or voice.
use: Invoke this skill for human-facing writing. Match the genre, intended meaning, audience, and permitted degree of revision before changing the words.
modes: Build prose around a clear promise and the reader’s context.
Make the material clearer while preserving the author’s stance and voice.
Assess the draft’s meaning, structure, evidence, and reader effort.
prompt: Use writing-for-humans to revise this guide while preserving my voice.
note: Agent-facing instructions belong to the independent Writing for Agents skill. This package includes verbatim Stop Slop guidance.
origin: Includes Hardik Pandya’s Stop Slop, preserved in full, alongside Atlas’s guidance for readers, revision, and different writing formats.

name: Team Up
intro: Select subagent roles, models, and reasoning effort when delegation or isolated context materially helps.
use: Use when the work benefits from a team. Choose the smallest capable team and match each assignment to an available role.
modes: Prefer a fitting custom agent, respecting its fixed settings.
Select the lowest-cost reliable model and reasoning effort for the task.
Honor a requested model and resolve unavailable choices before dispatch.
prompt: Use team-up to choose a small team for implementing and reviewing this feature.
note: Delegation is a choice based on the work, rather than a default requirement for every task.

name: Tracking Implementation
summary: Keep the state of a build easy to resume.
intro: Maintain a durable implementation record alongside the chosen executor, with progress, validation, and review evidence.
use: Use when you explicitly ask to track work or resume an existing implementation record. A request to implement alone does not activate tracking.
modes: Create the smallest useful implementation record from the supplied work context.
Keep execution state and evidence current alongside the executor.
Read the existing record and source material before continuing.
prompt: Use tracking-implementation to track this build alongside the executor.
note: The executor performs the work; Tracking records its state. A local check, commit, push, and acceptance remain separate evidence.
origin: Uses HumanLayer’s Show Me to shape implementation records. Atlas supplies the tracking state, evidence requirements, and review workflow.

name: Atlas Setup
summary: Check what an installed Atlas package still needs.
intro: Identify missing independent dependencies for the Atlas skills installed on the current host.
use: Invoke after installing selected Atlas packages. Setup checks the dependency registry and distinguishes unavailable skills from installed but inaccessible ones.
modes: Read the installed skill inventory and relevant dependency conditions.
Show each source, affected package, requirement, and installation command.
After an authorized installation, check availability to the intended host.
prompt: Use atlas-setup to check the dependencies for my installed Atlas skills.
note: Setup is a dependency check. It installs selected dependencies only when you authorize it; it is not a full-stack installer.
